title: GEO: Generative Engine Optimization
summary: Foundational academic paper (KDD 2024) that defines Generative Engine Optimization and introduces GEO-bench, a benchmark of diverse queries paired with web sources. The authors report that content-level methods can raise visibility in generative engine responses by up to 40%, with effectiveness varying by domain.

title: AI features and your website (Google Search Central)
summary: Google's official documentation says AI Overviews and AI Mode may use query fan-out, issuing multiple related searches to find a wider set of supporting pages. It states that no extra technical requirements or special markup apply beyond being indexed and snippet-eligible, and that AI feature traffic is counted in the Search Console Web search type. Preview controls (nosnippet, max-snippet, noindex) apply.

title: AI in Search Reduces Publisher Referrals Without Improving User Experience: Experimental Evidence
summary: Preregistered field experiment (preprint, not peer reviewed) with 1,100 US participants on Google Search. Removing AI Overviews and AI Mode raised click-through to publishers, while an AI Mode-only experience lowered it and reduced trust in Google. Secondary coverage reports roughly -18.8 points of external clicks under forced AI Mode and +8.8 points when AI features were hidden; the abstract itself gives no effect sizes.

title: New opportunities, control and insights for website owners
summary: Google announced Search Console reports on generative AI performance (impressions, pages and countries, no click data) and a toggle to opt a site out of AI Overviews, AI Mode and AI Overviews in Discover. Opting out removes traffic and impressions from those features and does not affect regular rankings. Rolled out first in the UK, and by Google's note reached all sites worldwide by 2026-08-31.

title: Google AI Overviews & AI Mode 0.9% Click-Through Rate, Opt Out Study Says
summary: Search Engine Roundtable reports a single-site opt-out test by Cyrus Shepard using Google's new AI opt-out control. He estimates about 0.9% CTR on AI impressions, which were about 8% of the site's impressions, and saw regular organic clicks fall as well. The author and the article both stress the sample is very small and the organic-drop explanation is interpretation.

title: Fan-outs per prompt by engine
summary: Vendor study (Peec AI) of about 5 million query fan-outs collected 1-21 April 2026. According to Peec, Perplexity averages 1.4 fan-outs per prompt, ChatGPT 2.1 and Grok 6.8; ChatGPT adds terms such as best, top and reviews, while Perplexity mostly reruns a cleaned-up query.

title: ChatGPT May Scrape Google, but the Results Don't Match
summary: Ahrefs compared citations from ChatGPT and Perplexity with Google's top 100 for about 3,311 short-tail keywords. According to Ahrefs, Perplexity URLs matched Google's top 10 in 65% of cases versus 10% for ChatGPT (7% long-tail, 6.8% fan-out), and ChatGPT cited ranking domains about three times more often than ranking pages. Ahrefs hypothesises a ChatGPT re-ranking layer.

title: Does schema markup improve AI citations? (Ahrefs study)
summary: According to Ahrefs, 1,885 pages that added JSON-LD between August 2025 and March 2026 showed no meaningful citation lift against matched controls on any platform, and a 4.6% drop on Google AI Overviews. Both groups were already declining, so the drop is hard to attribute to schema; the study cannot say whether schema helps pages not yet cited. A separate test cited by Ahrefs found tested systems read visible HTML and ignored JSON-LD.

title: OpenAI Says Robots.txt May Not Apply To ChatGPT's Fetch Bot
summary: OpenAI's crawler documentation says ChatGPT-User, which fetches pages when a user asks, may not follow robots.txt because the visit is user-initiated. TollBit's H1 2026 report, cited by SEJ, found about 15% of identified AI page-fetchers on European sites reached disallowed URLs. OAI-SearchBot is the agent that governs ChatGPT search inclusion, and Cloudflare planned default blocking of training and agent crawlers on new ad-supported domains from 15 September.

title: Sitecore acquires Scrunch to help brands influence discovery and buying decisions in the AI-search era
summary: Sitecore announced on 3 June 2026 the acquisition of AI visibility vendor Scrunch, with no price disclosed (Bloomberg reportedly put it near 225 million dollars). Scrunch's Agent Experience Platform is to be integrated into Sitecore's content workflows. Customer results in the release (Akamai +364% appearances in AI answers, +218% citations) are vendor-stated.

title: Profound raises 180M dollars Series D at 1.8B valuation
summary: Profound announced on 15 September 2026 a 180M dollar Series D at a 1.8B dollar valuation, co-led by Sequoia and Kleiner Perkins, less than seven months after a 96M dollar Series C. The company says it serves over 1,000 enterprise brands and is adding an AI Marketer agent orchestrator and Ads Studio for AI search ads. All figures are company-stated.
